clue.text: Model beginning to pose has very poor clothing

annotationWithheld.why: Model beginning to pose has very poor clothing (7): P (beginning to pose) is clear, but no reading of 'has very poor clothing' gives ARAGON; the RAG inside PA...ON is likely, yet PA and ON have no sound source in the clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Model beginning to pose has very poor clothing

clue.text: Harmless pill, gratifyingly effective?

parts.note: a dummy tablet that does no harm yet pleases the patient, the Latin name meaning 'I shall please'

explanation.surface: A drug that does no harm and works pleasingly well.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin name means 'I shall please', which is why the clue calls the pill gratifyingly effective: it works only because the patient believes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy medicine given for its psychological effect is the usual sense of the word.

clue.text: About to spring on journalist, but recoiled

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to bound is to spring or leap
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is pounced on and flinches back.
explanation.definitionFit: To bounce back after striking something is to spring back, synonym of recoil.

clue.text: Information about art-form

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Facts relating to a branch of the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information or the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A category of artistic work, such as the novel or opera, is a style or kind of art.

clue.text: Modern house for an Englishman in the north-east

parts.note: new means modern
the saying 'an Englishman's home is his castle'

explanation.surface: A new home built for an Englishman living in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'an Englishman's home is his castle' makes CASTLE his house. NEWCASTLE upon Tyne is the main city of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is located in that region of England, so the place is described by where it lies.

clue.text: Sort of turn in E London which is widely admired

indicators.note: the turn's letter goes inside the place name, so in signals one inside the other

parts.note: Poplar is a district of East London
a U-turn is a sort of turn

explanation.surface: A dance move done in the East End that everyone likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside POPLAR, a district of East London. 'Sort of turn' gives U, from U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something liked and approved of by many people is well liked, the plain sense of the word.

clue.text: Purpose of police duty

explanation.surface: What a police officer's job is really for.
explanation.definitionFit: The aim of an action is its object; point duty is a police officer's task of directing traffic at a junction.

clue.text: Simon pretended to get ribbon

parts.note: the apostle Simon was renamed Peter
sham means pretended, fake

explanation.surface: Simon faked it to win a ribbon.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostle Simon was called Peter by Jesus, so Simon gives PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff corded ribbon used for hatbands and waistbands carries this name.

clue.text: Before end of day diver becomes crazy

indicators.note: one piece comes before the other in the answer

parts.note: the loon is a diving bird, the North American name for the diver

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of day

explanation.surface: A diver goes mad before the day is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' puts LOON ahead of Y, the last letter of 'day'. The diver is the bird, not a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Loony is informal for mad or insane.

clue.text: Chatterbox a sort of government notice made nervous

parts.note: a rattle is an old word for an incessant talker
a D-notice is a British government request not to publish something

explanation.surface: A gossip and an official notice unsettle someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A D-notice is a British government request asking the press not to report a security matter, so the notice is a 'sort' of D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shaken or unnerved is the informal meaning.

clue.text: Saint takes first-class return from Balkan country

indicators.note: takes means removes, so letters are taken away from the country

parts.note: Albania is in the Balkans

indicators.note: return means the letters for first-class are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, read as AI

explanation.surface: A holy man comes back first-class from Albania.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 read as letters is AI, and 'return' turns it to IA; 'takes' removes IA from ALBANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban was the first British Christian martyr, a canonised saint.

clue.text: Wait outside Ascot for a change of clothing

indicators.note: the word wait is placed around the other letters
the letters of Ascot are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Wait outside the racecourse while someone changes clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' scrambles the racecourse name into STCOA, and 'outside' wraps the word wait round it. Ascot is an English racecourse; 'change of clothing' disguises the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless garment worn over a shirt is an item of dress.

clue.text: Overflowing with joy at new UN beer-tax

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone delighted at a new United Nations tax on beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges UN BEER TAX into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being full of high spirits and lively enthusiasm is a synonym for brimming with delight.

clue.text: Wager gold when backing, like a sovereign

indicators.note: backing means the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: to lay is to bet or wager
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Betting gold on a backed horse, like a king would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when backing' turns the whole bet-plus-gold string right round, giving LAYOR backwards. OR is gold in heraldry, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertaining to a monarch or king is what regal or kingly means.

clue.text: I don't get mixed up with gossip

indicators.note: mixed up means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to be involved in rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get mixed up' rearranges I DONT. On dit is French for 'one says'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning 'they say', used in English for a piece of hearsay.

clue.text: The game is to upset mine with union backing

parts.note: to tip is to upset or overturn
and means with, together with

indicators.note: backing means the union's letters are read backwards

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen

explanation.surface: The plan is to sabotage a mine with the union's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NUR, the National Union of Railwaymen, into RUN. Tip and run is an informal form of cricket where the batter must run whenever the ball is hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual cricket variant is a game, named for its rule of running on every hit.

clue.text: Charming utterance but inflammable

explanation.surface: A lucky saying that is also flammable.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is a charm against bad luck; as a noun it is dry rotten wood that catches fire easily, used as tinder.

clue.text: Badly behaved mongrel

explanation.surface: A badly behaved dog of no pedigree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-mannered from poor upbringing; also of impure breed, as a cross-bred dog is.

clue.text: It's a cello arrangement for swing.

indicators.note: an arrangement of music, here of the letters, which are reordered

explanation.surface: A cello piece arranged in swing style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges ITS A CELLO. Swing is the verb, not the jazz style.
explanation.definitionFit: To move back and forth regularly, like a pendulum, is to sway.

clue.text: Plot extended to cover a bunk?

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
spread means extended or stretched out

explanation.surface: A garden plot stretched out to cover a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: BED is a garden plot, so the wordplay hides the bed it covers.
explanation.definitionFit: The covering laid over a bed is meant to hide a bunk, with the question mark flagging that a bunk is one kind of bed.

clue.text: A god is said to be our supporter

indicators.note: said signals the letters are spoken aloud

parts.note: a backer is a supporter, plus 'us' for our

explanation.surface: A deity is said to be on our side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is said to be' marks a sound-alike: 'backer us' (one who backs us) sounds like the Roman god of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of wine is a deity.

clue.text: Virile Scot helped leader, nothing more

parts.note: Mac is a nickname for a Scotsman

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Scotsman helped the leader, and did nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes H, the first letter of 'helped'; MAC is a common nickname for a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressively masculine and manly is the usual meaning.

clue.text: As bowman he'd be in the forefront of a row

definitions.text: As bowman he'd be in the forefront of a row

parts.words: As bowman he'd be in the forefront of a row
parts.note: the bowman is the rower sitting nearest the bow, and row is rowing, not a line or a quarrel

explanation.surface: An archer at the front of a line or quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowman suggests an archer and row a line, but the bow is the front of a boat and the row is a spell of rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower in the bow seat sits at the front of the crew, so he leads the boat.

clue.text: Stop or pass on

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between halting or going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' looks like a single phrase meaning hand over, but COL is a mountain pass, followed by ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark is a stop in old printing terms.

clue.text: A refreshing if unsatisfactory type of answer

definitions.text: A refreshing if unsatisfactory type of answer

parts.words: A refreshing if unsatisfactory type of answer
parts.note: a sour citrus fruit used in cool drinks, and slang for a dud, as when 'the answer is' this fruit

explanation.surface: A satisfying yet disappointing reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit is refreshing in drinks, and in slang it is a dud; 'the answer's a lemon' is an old phrase for a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus fruit flavours cool drinks, and in slang it names something useless or disappointing.

clue.text: Not even a soldier

explanation.surface: Not quite a real soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven or not smooth; also a fighter not in the regular army, such as a guerrilla.

clue.text: Singular bridge achievement in the Muslim world

parts.note: I is the singular first person, and I is one
a slam is winning all or all but one of the tricks in bridge

explanation.surface: A single success at the bridge table in Muslim lands.
explanation.walkthrough: A slam in the card game bridge is taking twelve or thirteen tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: The religion of Muslims is also used for the community of believers worldwide.

clue.text: Type of snake in a stage menagerie?

explanation.surface: A kind of snake in a theatrical zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass snake is a legless lizard; Tennessee Williams's play The Glass Menagerie features a collection of figurines.

clue.text: Usually mother is a supporter of independence

parts.note: the clue suggests who normally runs the household: the parent who governs the family house

explanation.surface: Mothers usually support independence.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is whoever rules the home, usually mother; as one hyphenated term it is someone backing self-government, as for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer of self-government for a region, such as Irish devolution campaigners, supports independence.

clue.text: What wakes us up in jolly style

parts.note: à la means in the style of
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: Something that rouses us cheerfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective, but it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine (RM). 'in ... style' is à la, in the manner of.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock bell or signal that rouses sleepers is the warning device.

clue.text: Work for Labour, for example

parts.note: the word work can stand for the word labour, and the capital L pretends this is the political party

explanation.surface: Campaigning for the Labour Party, say.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L suggests canvassing for Britain's Labour Party; in fact 'work' is a word of the same meaning as 'labour'.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the same meaning as another, as work is for labour, is the term described.

clue.text: Make out record given with key to Navy

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
E is a musical key
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Distinguishing a record supplied with the navy's key.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive or detect something with difficulty is the synonym.
